messages:
alice: Heads up — seeing repeated ECC/Xid warnings on gpu-node-07 for the last hour. Looks like a flaky card.
ben: I can see spikes in DCGM. Are we auto-draining on ECC bursts right now?
devops-bot: Alert: gpu.ecc_errors > 10 in 5m for node=gpu-node-07. Suggested action: inspect / initiate remediation.
carla: We only have a manual playbook today. We should design a safe automated flow: cordon -> drain (grace) -> taint + quarantine -> schedule replacement if needed.
alice: yes, but add noise protection: require sustained signal (e.g., 3 consecutive windows) before any auto-action. Dont want a driver reset to cause churn.
ben: Proposed remediation flow: 
1) DCGM exporter -> Prom alert severity=warning on anomaly. 
2) remediation-runner dry-run evaluates node health, PDBs, and pool saturation. 
3) If sustained (3/5m) and PDBs allow: kubectl cordon + taint gpu.redwood/evacuate=true:NoSchedule. 
4) kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 --timeout=10m. 
5) notify #eng-infra + SRE oncall and create ops ticket with metrics snapshot. 
6) If drain fails -> mark unschedulable, schedule reprovision from spare pool.
carla: For Slurm-managed batch nodes use: `scontrol update NodeName=<node> State=DRAIN Reason="gpu-health"` and trigger checkpoint/kick policies.
alice: For long-running model servers, attempt graceful eviction via sidecar: send SIGTERM, allow 120s to flush KV caches, then force.
sre-oncall: How do we avoid false positives from transient Xid 13 resets?
ben: Heuristic: require either (ECC delta > 0 AND Xid >= 5 within 3m) OR ECC delta > configurable threshold. Also require 3 consecutive alert windows.
carla: Add a circuit-breaker: abort automation if >5 nodes would be drained concurrently or >10% of a pool drained in last 30m.
alice: Telemetry requirement: every automated drain must create an ops-triage ticket with DCGM snapshot, dmesg, `nvidia-smi -q`, and remediation status. Include cost delta for replacement (spot vs reserved).
ben: Example k8s commands the remediation job will run:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-07
kubectl drain gpu-node-07 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 --timeout=10m
kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-07 gpu.redwood/failed=true:NoSchedule
```
And for Slurm:
```
scontrol update NodeName=gpu-node-07 State=DRAIN Reason=\"ecc-errors\"
```
carla: Testing plan: run in staging with fault-injector pod to simulate ECC/Xid. Dry-run webhook posts to #eng-infra for 24h before any auto action.
alice: Feature flags: auto-drain-staging (on), auto-drain-canary (10% of nodes), auto-drain-prod (off by default).
sre-oncall: Also add an emergency kill-switch and a small canary window (start with 1 node per pool). Ill add escalation steps in the runbook.
ben: Implementation note: remediation-runner should respect PDBs and prefer binpack-aware evictions (avoid evacuating many nodes in same AZ).
carla: Quarantine process: new reprovisioned node lands in quarantine pool with label gpu.quarantine=true, then manual soak tests; reenable by removing taint and uncordon after soak.
alice: Ownership: @carla will update docs/playbook; @ben will open PR for automation and feature flags; Ill own the first-responder role during canary rollout.
devops-bot: Scheduled job created: gpu-health-remediation-runner (canary)  runs dry-runs in staging every 15m.
carla: ETA staging rollout EOD tomorrow. Will post updates and attach test logs. :thumbsup: 
alice: Great. Keep canary small and watch for noisy signals for 48h. If anything odd, page SRE-oncall immediately.
